issues.detail: The Hebrew 'לֶֽאֱלִיָּ֔תָה' is a proper name 'Eliathah' (a Levite, 1 Chronicles 25:4, 27), not '以利亞' (Elijah). The Chinese renders it as '以利亞' (Elijah), swapping the name. Also, the Hebrew 'לְעֶשְׂרִים' means 'for the twentieth' (referring to the twentieth division/course), not 'twenty-two' (עשרים ושנים). The Chinese '共有二十二人' (twenty-two people) misreads the number; the Hebrew says 'for Eliathah, his sons and his brothers, twelve' (שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר = twelve), not twenty-two. The Chinese omits 'twelve' and adds 'twenty-two'.
